$comment: R6.45. Every top-level directory under conformance/ is named here, with its vector count and the profiles its vectors may declare. Every conformance runner SHALL load this file and fail when it disagrees with what is on disk. A family a runner does not enumerate contributes no assurance while looking, in a passing test-run log, exactly like one that does -- and every runner hard-codes its family list in source, so a family added to the corpus is invisible to each implementation until that implementation is separately edited. This file is what makes that omission fail.

directories.name: red-team
directories.note: Detector corpus for R10.11's measurement (Appendix L), not canonicalization vectors. Listed so that its absence from every runner is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.

directories.name: retrieval
directories.note: The held-out query set behind Phase 3's 'dedupe measured on a real query set' and R10.5's canaries (conformance/retrieval/README.md). Not a vector family: curia-testis has no embedding capability and cannot run it, so it is enumerated by Curia.Application.Tests alone, and listed here so that is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.
